key_insight: Doc2Harness shows that for long-horizon coding agents, the quality of the surrounding harness can be as important as the model itself, and harness engineering is still very hard even for frontier LLMs.
engineering_relevance: This benchmark gives practitioners a deterministic way to test whether a model can build robust agent scaffolding that works across isolated containers and realistic multi-step tool workflows.
method: Stage 1: a build model receives an interface-only contract skeleton plus a consolidated development document and constructs a candidate harness in an isolated container.
Stage 2: the frozen harness is executed in separate containers per test case and driven end-to-end by a scripted mock model.
Scoring uses four observable channels: model requests, files on disk, process exit code, and command output, with positive controls to prevent vacuous passes.
evidence_signal: Across 19 frontier models, 3 independent builds each, and 328 test cases, the top model reached 53.05% pass rate while the weakest was 27.44%, indicating substantial remaining failure modes.
watch_item: Because Stage 1 is build-time and Stage 2 is fully frozen, results may depend on how well the benchmark documents and isolates cross-cutting behavior that real harnesses often implement incrementally.
paper_title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
